cases.question: How many PTO days do new employees get, and can unused days roll over?

gold_chunk: carry over up to 5 unused PTO days

answer.content:
New full-time employees receive **18 days of PTO per calendar year**, accruing at **1.5 days per month** starting on the first day of employment; part-time employees accrue PTO in proportion to their scheduled hours. [S1]

Employees can carry over **up to 5 unused PTO days** into the next calendar year, but must use them by **March 31**; other unused days are forfeited on **December 31** and are not paid out, except where local law requires a payout. [S1]

LRK-4471 was the August platform outage: on August 12, 2026, a failed database migration caused a 9-hour outage of Larkspur’s forecasting platform, affecting 41 customers. [S1]

- **Root cause:** A schema change was applied without a tested rollback plan. [S1]
- **Cost:** Service credits, overtime and remediation work cost $120k in total. [S1]
- **Follow-up actions:** Every migration now requires a tested rollback plan, schema changes roll out to 5% of customers first, and a public status page was launched on September 1. [S1]

- **Status:** The October 2, 2026 board update said remediation was complete and follow-up actions were on track; it described the outage as the most serious incident this year. [S5]

cases.question: What is the remote work stipend? Has it changed?

gold_chunk: remote work stipend of $500 per year

answer.content:
The remote work stipend is **$750 per year**, effective October 1, 2026; the board increased it from **$500 per year**. [S2]

- The January 15, 2026 handbook still lists $500 per year, but the more recent October 2, 2026 board update records the increase and says People Operations will update the handbook in its next edition. [S1][S2][S4]
- The stipend helps cover internet, furniture and other home-office costs; the handbook says it is paid in the January payroll and prorated for employees who join during the year. [S1]

cases.question: Which vendor is cheaper over three years, and which has the stronger SLA?

answer.content:
**BrightPath is cheaper over three years at the quoted subscription rates, while CoreLink has the stronger SLA based on uptime, service credits and support coverage.** CoreLink’s subscription pricing is locked for only the first 24 months, so its actual three-year cost is not guaranteed by these sources. [S1][S2][S3]

- **BrightPath:** $420,000 + 3 × $60,000 = **$600,000**, excluding applicable taxes. [S1]
- **CoreLink:** $380,000 + 3 × $95,000 = **$665,000**, assuming the quoted annual rate remains unchanged in year 3. [S2]
- **Difference:** $665,000 − $600,000 = **$65,000** in BrightPath’s favor under that assumption. [S1][S2]

**SLA comparison:**
- **CoreLink:** 99.9% monthly uptime; credits of 10% of the monthly subscription fee for each 0.1% below target, capped at 50%; 24/7 support. [S2]
- **BrightPath:** 99.5% monthly uptime; credits of 5% of that month’s subscription fee for each 0.5% below target; business-hours support (8:00 to 18:00 Mountain Time), with a 4-hour response target for priority 1 issues. [S1][S3]

cases.question: And after three years?
turns: How many PTO days do new employees get, and can unused days roll over?

answer.content:
After three years of continuous service, full-time employees receive **20 PTO days per year**: 18 days + 2 additional days = 20 days; the increase applies from the first full month after the employee's third work anniversary. [S1]

Up to **5 unused PTO days** may roll over into the next calendar year and must be used by **March 31**; any other unused days are forfeited on **December 31** and are not paid out, except where local law requires a payout. [S1]
